# Observational Constraints on Interacting Dark Matter Model Without Dark Energy
## Abstract
The interacting dark matter (IDM) scenario allows for the acceleration of the Universe without Dark Energy. We constrain the IDM model by using the newly revised observational data including $H \left(\right. z \left.\right)$H(z) data and Union2 SNe Ia via the Markov chain Monte Carlo method. When mimicking the $\Lambda$Λ CDM model, we obtain a more stringent upper limit to the effective annihilation term at $\kappa C_{1} \approx 10^{- 3.4} \left(G y r\right)^{- 1}$κ C 1​≈1 0−3.4 Gyr−1, and a tighter lower limit to the relevant mass of Dark Matter particles at $M_{x} \approx 10^{- 8.6} G e v$M x​≈1 0−8.6 Gev. When mimicking the $w$w CDM model, we find that the effective equation of state of IDM is consistent with the concordance $\Lambda$Λ CDM model and appears to be most consistent with the effective phantom model with a constant EoS for which $w < - 1$w<−1.
